The Silent Explorers

Messages From Machines We Left Behind

Continue keeps your progress. Start fresh clears it so you (or a friend) can begin from zero.

Out on the Moon, on Mars and far out in deep space, 14 NASA explorers sit silent. Some of them are twins, like Spirit and Opportunity. Their missions ended — but their memories didn't.

📖 Fact or story? The machines, missions and facts in this game are real.
When a machine talks, look for 🛰 NASA fact (from NASA's NSSDCA spacecraft catalogue and mission records) or 💬 Story voice (the machine “talking” in an imagined voice). Aira, Grandpa, ECHO and the people in the memory recordings are made-up story characters — look for the “story character” tag.

🗺️ Everything else we left behind

A quick guide to every machine NASA has left on the Moon, on Mars and out in deep space. Tap one to read about it, then press ▶ to play its mission.

🛰️ Find any spacecraft yourself: the NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA) is NASA's public catalogue of everything sent into space: its mission details, where it ended up and whether it still works.

All memories restored

Thank you, explorer.

You landed softly on the Moon, drove across it, raced a dust storm on Mars, dug for ice and listened to a planet tremble. You helped ECHO remember who it was. And all 14 silent explorers, from Eagle on the Moon to the Pioneer twins drifting towards the stars, are waiting to be remembered too.

Some of these machines will never move again. Others still circle distant worlds or drift out of the solar system. But every rock they touched, every photo they sent, every quake they heard and every planet they found is still teaching us. Now their stories travel on with you.

"No explorer is forgotten — as long as someone tells their story."
